players.name: Josh Allen
notes: The Keep #1 · average 1.7 across 10 Superflex boards
The Board #1 on the long proprietary aggregate
Redraft PPR #28 (Yates 28)
Redraft Standard #29
plus: Seven-board Superflex lock: Keep #1, average 2.0.
Dual-threat floor still separates him from every other aging QB1.
minus: Turns 31 in 2026 — first real dynasty age tax on a perennial 1.01.
Yates PPR has him in the late 20s; 1QB redraft does not pay the SF premium.
grafs: Josh Allen is still the player Ball Keep is built around. Seven sources — PFN, Dynasty Nerds, FantasyPros, KeepTradeCut, and the three X experts we track — all have him inside the top four Superflex assets, and the average lands at 2.0. That is not a recency spike. It is the market admitting that a quarterback who runs, extends, and finishes in the end zone is the safest way to keep a Superflex roster relevant through 2029.

The 2025 tape is the same argument on film: launch-point throws and designed keepers, with the Bills still built to let him create when protection breaks. Redraft boards (Field Yates has him in the high 20s) treat him as a mid QB1 because 1QB leagues do not have to pay the second-starter tax. Dynasty Superflex does. That split is the whole point of The Keep.

The minus is honest: he will be 31 this season, and the first time a 23-year-old passer (Maye) outranks him on a short list, the age conversation gets louder. We are not selling the 1.01 for that. We are naming it. If you are rebuilding past 2028, Maye is the bet. If you are trying to win the next two title windows, Allen is still the chip you do not put in a trade calculator for fun.

grafs: Drake Maye is the dynasty argument of 2026. Three of our short expert lists (FantasyPros ECR, Andrew Erickson, Pat Fitzmaurice) rank him the Superflex 1.01, Derek Brown has him second, and the long boards (PFN, Dynasty Nerds) park him third behind only Allen. The Keep average is 2.43. That is a 23-year-old passer being priced like a finished product.

The 2025 film is why. The Can't-Miss clip we embedded is the AFC run in miniature: Maye dropping a touchdown and a receiver finishing like a superhero. New England's offense finally looks like a place where a long-striding quarterback can push the ball and scramble without the supporting cast being a weekly apology. Superflex managers who waited on the 2024 draft capital got paid.

The pushback is KeepTradeCut at six and redraft boards that still treat him as a high-end QB2 in 1QB. That is useful. It means you can still find a manager who thinks Allen/Lamar/Hurts are 'safer' and will overpay in picks to move down. Ball Keep's stance: the experts have moved. The startup ADP will follow. Do not be the last one holding the 2024 'he might be Caleb-tier' take.
